chunks: It is narrated from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Bāqir عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “What prevents the believer from taking a spouse? Perhaps Allah will provide him with a soul who will make the earth weighty with ‘There is no god but Allah.’”

key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنَ: the believer, the person being encouraged toward marriage
key_terms.بِلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: the declaration of tawhid, affirming that there is no god but Allah
key_terms.يَتَّخِذَ أَهْلًا: to take a spouse or establish a household
key_terms.يَرْزُقَهُ: to provide him or grant him sustenance

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the virtue of marriage and having children in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith encourages the believer toward marriage by highlighting the hope of righteous offspring. Its significance lies in connecting family formation with the spread of tawhid, as future generations may fill the earth with the testimony of faith.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4340 - It is narrated from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (as) that the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) said:
"What prevents a believer from taking a spouse? Perhaps Allah (swt) will grant him offspring who will fill the earth with 'There is no god but Allah (swt).'"
